description:
You are sixteen when the plague empties half your village, and the fields your neighbours once worked are suddenly, strangely, yours for the taking. Follow one Englishwoman's whole life in the decades after the Black Death — a marriage priced in shillings, a night of labour that could have ended in silence, and a slow, unglamorous kind of freedom no peasant before her ever held.

A calm, unhurried second-person story to relax or fall asleep to, built on real manor records, wages, laws and events from fourteenth-century England.
era_setting: An open-field manor village in Oxfordshire, England, modeled on the surviving records of Cuxham and Halesowen, about 1350-1400: timber and wattle-and-daub cottages, undyed grey and brown wool clothing, muddy lanes, a small stone parish church, and wide barley strips left half-empty by the Black Death.

shorts.title: They Priced Her Marriage in Shillings #shorts
shorts.description: In medieval England, an unfree peasant woman's marriage had a literal price tag. #history #medievalengland #yourlifeas

scenes.narration: In medieval England, an unfree woman needed her lord's permission, and a fee, just to marry.
Her father haggles over that fee the way another man haggles over a plough ox.
She stands at the back of the hall, hearing her own worth argued over in shillings.
Years later, that same court starts murmuring about freezing the wages her family finally earns.
When the roads fill with angry men marching on London, her husband chooses to stay home.
By the time her own daughter weds, no steward argues over any fee at all.
Her daughter inherits a freedom she never had — this is the full story of how.

shorts.title: The Night the Midwife Was Sent For #shorts
shorts.description: One agonising night decides everything for a peasant mother in plague-era England. #history #childbirth #yourlifeas

scenes.narration: Her pains begin at dusk, and by midnight someone is running through the dark for her husband.
The labour goes on for hours, one candle burning down into the next.
Near dawn she stops fearing the pain, and starts fearing only one terrible silence.
Then the cry comes, thin and furious and alive, and the whole room breathes again.
Her husband, still smelling of the field, kneels to touch the baby's fist for the first time.
Half-asleep, she finally lets herself grieve the mother who isn't there to see this.
She names her daughter that night, never guessing the world her child will grow up to inherit.

editor_notes: The critic forced a multi-year time-skip before the marriage (fixing a timeline clash with our own research on marriage age), a hedge on the debated wage-statute claim, and a genuine open loop at the end of chapter 3 instead of an early-resolved theme.
